name: Abel Evans
bio: Abel Evans (1679–1737) was an English clergyman and wit, a member of St John's College, Oxford, and an acquaintance of Pope. He was known in his own day for his epigrams and for Latin and English verse.
His best-remembered lines are the mock epitaph on the architect Sir John Vanbrugh, whose buildings included Blenheim Palace.

poems.title: On Sir John Vanbrugh
poems.author: Abel Evans
poems.text:
Under this stone, Reader, survey
Dead Sir John Vanbrugh's house of clay.
Lie heavy on him, Earth! for he
Laid many heavy loads on thee!
